title: Compare the prediction with the plotted evidence
prompt:
# Codex PPT Slide Image Prompt

## Canvas
{
  "type": "16:9 full-slide PowerPoint image",
  "language": "English",
  "slide_number": 10,
  "render_slide_number": false

## Deck Goal
Teach Year-2 physics students to move from a familiar vertical-motion model to named MATLAB variables, sampled arrays, element-wise operations, a labelled plot, and one executable physical validation check.

## Required Background
{
  "deck_context": {
    "source_summary": "This Week 01 lecture repairs uncertain MATLAB foundations through one familiar model: a ball launched vertically upward with air resistance neglected. Students predict the motion, identify variables and units, create a time array, use MATLAB indexing and element-wise operators, plot height against time, and validate the known launch value.",
    "core_claim": "A physical model becomes trustworthy computational evidence only when its variables, arrays, operations, plot, and validation check stay connected.",
    "canonical_terms": [
      "vertical motion",
      "physical model",
      "variables and units",
      "time array",
      "MATLAB indexing starts at 1",
      "element-wise operators",
      "labelled plot",
      "boundary check",
      "physical interpretation"
    ],
    "locked_model": {
      "equation": "y(t) = y0 + v0 t - (1/2) g t^2",
      "assumptions": [
        "upward is positive",
        "air resistance is neglected"
      ],
      "values": {
        "y0": "0 m",
        "v0": "20 m s^-1",
        "g": "9.81 m s^-2",
        "time": "0:0.1:4 s"
      },
      "predictions": [
        "starts at y = 0 m",
        "rises to one maximum",
        "falls back toward the launch height"
      ],
      "required_validation": "y(0) = 0 m, represented in MATLAB as y_m(1)"
    }
  },
  "slide_local_context": "Create a complete qualitative teaching graphic from the locked vertical-motion predictions. Show a smooth height-versus-time curve with no invented numerical axes, ticks, or values. Attach each short label directly beside the curve segment it describes, using a tiny local marker or short tick rather than long crossing leader lines. This is a conceptual graph-reading illustration, not strict numerical evidence."
}

## Source Image Rules
No supplied plot is required. Generate the complete conceptual curve and labels as one coherent slide image; do not invent quantitative axes, numerical data, or measurement claims.

## Constraints
[
  "Make every label-to-curve relationship immediately obvious with direct adjacency or a very short local connector.",
  "Do not use the old MATLAB plot or long crossing leader lines.",
  "Do not add numerical ticks, values, or a fabricated legend.",
  "No slide number."
]

## Style Reference Rule
Use Image 1 as the approved sample-slide style reference. Match its palette, typography mood, density, texture, and overall visual identity. Do not copy its exact layout unless this slide's layout explicitly asks for it.

## Input Image Handling Rules
For any input image marked as a strict input asset, include it visibly and preserve its content. Do not redraw, replace, relabel, or invent a similar figure. Scale and crop only as needed for composition while keeping the important labels, arrows, data, and relationships recognizable.

## Universal Constraints
- The final image itself must contain the title and key points.
- Render Chinese text exactly and legibly; avoid garbled characters.
- Keep the confirmed deck style consistent while varying layout by slide role.
- No watermark, unrelated logo, or extra slide number.
